top.title: Brady Hart gets start as Texas A&M makes change at quarterback for Oklahoma game
top.description: Brady Hart got his first start for Texas A&M on Saturday at Oklahoma, replacing an ineffective Marcel Reed in the Aggies' next-to-last game of the regular season. (Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) NORMAN, Okla. - Mike Elko has opted for a change in quarterback for Texas A& M 's final road game of a disappointing 2026 season. Brady Hart's first career start Saturday against Oklahoma comes one week after he received his most meaningful playing time of the season. The sophomore quarterback entered the Aggies' 22-7 loss to Tennessee last week with under 3 minutes remaining and completed two of his three pass attempts for 22 yards before throwing an interception. Following the consistent struggles of returning starter Marcel Reed, Hart's entry received a standing ovation by fans at Kyle Field. A week later, Hart was handed the offense from the opening snap against an Oklahoma (6-4) defense which ranks fifth in the SEC in yards allowed (294.6). Hart had appeared in four games this season for the Aggies (4-6), completing 14 of 24 passes for 165 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. His most productive outing came in A&M's blowout win over The Citadel , when Hart completed 8 of 12 passes for 107 yards and a touchdown. He also had two carries for 8 yards. Saturday's change came after an increasingly rough stretch for an Aggie offense that entered the OU matchup ranked 13th in the SEC in total offense (341.2). A&M managed just 179 yards against Tennessee, never reached the red zone and scored seven points. Reed completed nine of 22 passes for 71 yards and an interception before Hart was put in the game. Elko took responsibility for the offense after the loss, calling it "inept" and "completely non-functional" while pushing back against the idea that the problems could be attributed solely to Reed. The opportunity in Norman put Hart in the middle of the Aggies' final push for bowl eligibility, needing to win their final two games in order to receive an invitation. top.title: Wilton field hockey scores with 52 seconds left to beat Branford for first CIAC title since 2015
top.description: Casey O'Connor, center, of Wilton and her teammates celebrate their 1-0 victory against Branford in the CIAC Class M Field Hockey Championship in Wethersfield on November 10, 2026. O'Connor scored the winning goal. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) WETHERSFIELD - Wilton field hockey player Maeve Ryder had barely gotten her cleat back on when the ball found her stick. She immediately sent in a hard cross, and Casey O'Connor was waiting to tip it over the goalie's head with 52 seconds left to play, giving No. 2 Wilton its first CIAC title in over a decade with a 1-0 win over No. 1 Branford on Saturday in the Class M final at Wethersfield High School. It is Wilton's seventh CIAC title but its first since 2015. O'Connor had just been released from a penalty and got herself in position to flick in the game-winning goal, while Ryder lost her shoe in a collision and had just pounded her foot back into it when she got the ball. "I came right off the penalty box and I knew we had less than a minute left and I knew we had to do this and end it because I was too tired to play 7 vs. 7," O'Connor said. "I stuck my stick out in front and I saw it going up. When it went in, I was ecstatic. It was so much fun." Wilton coach Leon Kerr said the play developed just as they practiced it, other than Ryder's shoe coming off. "We have been working on that with a packed circle and trying to put two forwards in there and getting the ball across and get a stick on it," Kerr said. "Once you get a stick on a hard pass, it will pop and we know that this goalie likes to go flat, so we worked on trying to pop the ball over her." O'Connor is one of 12 seniors on the Wilton team, making this run to a championship even more special. "This means the world," O'Connor said. "We have worked for this, and the coaches have done such a great job preparing us. It was a collective effort and everyone did their part." Wilton controlled much of the game, though Ellie Meyran of Branford broke out for several scoring chances without converting. Branford was playing in its third straight Class M title game and was the defending champion. "We have been resilient all season and it was unfortunate that goal came so late because it didn't give us a chance to respond," Branford coach Peter Frye said. "We knew this was going to be a really tight game and expected a one-goal game." Branford was playing in its 18th championship game, while Wilton was making its 12th trip to a final. top.title: Maple Leafs Take Sudden Drastic Step After 8th-Straight Loss
top.description: Jim Hiller Maple Leafs Getty Maple Leafs Jim Hiller Getty The Toronto Maple Leafs are in the midst of an eight-game losing skid after having dropped a 4-3 shootout decision against the struggling Los Angeles Kings on Thursday night. While they were finally able to break their pointless skid, they’ve still not won a single game in the month of November. Additionally, their six straight losses on home ice set a mark that hadn’t been seen in multiple decades. In a drastic step, the Maple Leafs have now brought in a renowned sports psychologist to try and turn the tide. Toronto Maple Leafs Bring In Renowned Sports Psychologist To Speak To The Organization Getty Maple Leafs Jim Hiller On Friday morning, the Maple Leafs were not only visited by Rory McIlroy, but also by sports psychologist Dr. Bob Rotella. McIlroy read the starting lineup in the dressing room prior to the game on Thursday night, and later visited again with the team the following day, along with Dr. Rotella, the author of multiple books, including the New York Times best seller “How Champions Think” in 2015. “If I can win the Masters, then the Leafs can win the Stanley Cup,” McIlroy said. “What an honour for us to have him,” Hiller said of the six-time major champion. “We got a chance to meet with him a little bit as coaches and then the players. If you are wondering what an athlete, a pro, a winner and all the things, you can add all the superlatives you want, that’s him. “He’s gone through some difficult times at certain times too and he just powered through so I think he’s just a great example for us right here right now.” Jim Hiller Addresses Job Security Hiller also addressed his job security amidst rumors that he could potentially be let go not even halfway into his first year with the club. “Not something I think about too much. I appreciate that John did that. My job is to win games. We haven’t won enough, so I’ll get them ready to win tomorrow (on Saturday against the Columbus Blue Jackets),” Hiller said. “Yeah, I mean, listen, we want to win. I told you that. I love hockey. I love winning. And when those two things collide, when you don’t win, it doesn’t feel very good. I’ve said that multiple times,” Hiller said. top.description: COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 7: Head Coach Ryan Day of the Ohio State Buckeyes talks with the referees during a timeout in the second quarter of the game against the Oregon Ducks at Ohio Stadium on November 7, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. The Match Lyon’s new head coach Carlos Vicens would be given a proper welcome to Ligue 1 with a trip to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy to face Carlo Ancelotti’s Lille. Coming out of the international break, Lille were in the runners-up spot and wanted to maintain the two-point gap with Paris Saint-Germain. It was a cagey start to the game, with neither side having much luck finding space within the box. Shots were largely restrained to tame efforts from outside the box. Nabil Bentaleb’s swipe wide for the hosts was almost bettered by Corentin Tolisso’s effort that forced Berke Özer into a stretching save. It took forty minutes for the game to come to life, with Mads Bidstrup firing home off the post from a messy moment of defending by Alexsandro. The centre-back, who so often looks composed at the back, got his first touch wrong in an interception in the box, allowing Corentin Tolisso to poke the ball to Bidstrup. Shortly after the restart, Lyon had the ball in the back of the net again when Abner Vinícius found Ernest Nuamah in the box. Ancelotti brought on Japanese international Ayase Ueda at half-time as he looked to give a shot in the arm to his flagging side. They were mostly restricted to efforts from distance, as Ngal’ayel Mukau, Bentaleb, and Nathan Ngoy each took turns trying to fire Les Dogues level. Olivier Giroud was thrown on as Lille searched for an equaliser, but it was not enough for a side that, despite their success in the league thus far, has struggled to consistently find the back of the net. There was desperation and chaos in the Lyon box in the final minutes, but it was not enough to force a last-gasp twist as Lyon held onto their narrow win and delivered Lille their first home defeat in the league this season. top.title: 49ers waive ex-Bills, Saints WR with 9,869 career receiving yards
top.description: 49ers waive ex-Bills, Saints WR with 9,869 career receiving yards originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers have needed wide receiver help this season, as they've dealt with a ridiculous string of injuries. But heading into Week 11, it appears they're getting healthy. Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel have been back, and now Mike Evans appears set to play in Sunday Night Football against the Minnesota Vikings . The return of these WRs, along with the trade for Keenan Allen, has really shaken up this WR room. One fallout of this WR room improving and getting healthier is a veteran wide receiver who's spent time with the Buffalo Bills and New Orleans Saints , Brandin Cooks, who the 49ers announced on Saturday was being waived prior to Week 11. 49ers waive WR Brandin Cooks prior to Week 11 "The following player has been waived: WR Brandin Cooks," the 49ers announced. "In addition, CB Nate Hobbs game status has been downgraded from questionable to out." San Francisco's WR room is getting healthier, and that's led the team to move on from Cooks this season. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, Keenan Allen, Jordan Watkins, and Jacob Cowing are all healthy for the 49ers right now. While this is an older WR room that does need depth, the 49ers do not need a seventh WR in Cooks, especially with De'Zhuan Stribling potentially coming back later this season as well. Cooks played in five games for the 49ers this season, catching five of his 10 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown. The 49ers are Cooks' seventh NFL franchise, and the most recent one after spending 2025 with the Saints and Bills. MORE : Grading NFL trade deadline debuts, from Kirk Cousins' Vikings return to Josh Downs' impressive day He has 9,869 receiving yards in his NFL career, only 131 yards away from reaching 10,000 for his career, which would be quite an accomplishment. Cooks also has 61 receiving touchdowns and 739 receptions on 1,145 targets in 178 games played in his 13-year NFL career that began with the Saints back in 2014 after being taken in Round 1 at No. 20 overall in the 2014 NFL Draft. If this is it for Cooks, he's had an incredible career. But with plenty of WR-needy teams around the NFL, Cooks, at 33 years old, could realistically sign somewhere this season and chase 10,000 receiving yards. A return to the Los Angeles Rams would make sense. But with the 49ers getting healthier in the wide receiver room, they've decided to move on from Cooks. He'll hit waivers, where he could be claimed by a team. If he clears, he'll be a free agent and could choose any team, including the 49ers, to sign with. top.description: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns Getty A 6-4 record is not, generally, cause for celebration in the NFL, but if you’re the coach of the Cleveland Browns and coming off two years in which the team scored eight total wins, it’s a lot more noteworthy. That’s where Browns coach Todd Monken is now, and all things considered, he has done a pretty good job. He has gotten something out of what had been the husk of Deshaun Watson’s career, he has managed to run an offense with an entirely new offensive line that includes two rookies, he has maximized two rookies and a second-year player as his top pass-catchers, he has kept the defense’s standard high despite trading away Myles Garrett and while teams like Dallas and Philadelphia have undergone much hand-wringing over having one first-year coordinator on staff, all three of Monken’s coordinators are first-timers, and doing just fine. All that makes the 6-4 that much more impressive. And Monken could be rewarded for that. Browns’ Todd Monken vs. 49ers’ Kyle Shanahan As of now, in fact, Monken is the favorite to win the NFL’s Coach of the Year Award here in 2026. Browns fans might roll their eyes at that–Kevin Stefanski won it with the Browns, twice, and his name does not evoke much fondness in Northeast Ohio. But it is an indication of how Monken is being viewed around the NFL. Monken opened the year as a plus-1,800 proposition for the award, tied for 10th among all coaches. top.title: Arsenal 'pained' by dropping points at Newcastle, says Arteta
top.description: Mikel Arteta's Arsenal were held 2-2 by Newcastle (ANDY BUCHANAN) Mikel Arteta said he could sense the anguish among his players despite opening up a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League with a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday. The Gunners missed the chance to extend their winning league run to six games after conceding twice in a careless spell just after half-time. Eberechi Eze's strike was scant reward for Arsenal's dominance in the first half. Goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw then put Arteta's men at risk of just a second defeat this season until Noni Madueke rescued a point. Arsenal moved six points clear of Brighton, who can close the gap to three with victory at Hull on Sunday, and Manchester City ahead of their trip to the Emirates Stadium next weekend. "We've been here six or seven years with me and it's the best we've played here by far and we have won a few times," said Arteta. "Today the margins should have been much, much bigger and they weren't. That's the pain that we are all feeling. It's not just me, it's a pain that the players are feeling, but immediately I could sense that and that's the standard that we need." Even more damaging than the loss of two points could be a shoulder injury to goalkeeper David Raya. The Spanish international was forced off shortly after Newcastle's second goal and would be a major loss if he is sidelined for a lengthy period. "Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is never good news," added Arteta. "He will get assessed now and he will probably have an MRI tomorrow to see what it is exactly because at the moment, I don't know." kca/nf

top.title: U17 World Cup: Patetuci hails opening win and squad strength
top.description: U17 World Cup: Patetuci hails opening win and squad strength Coach pleased with the team's approach Credits: Nelson Terme /CBF Brazil's men's U-17 national team opened their World Cup campaign with a 2-1 win over Ireland on Saturday (21) in Doha, Qatar. After the match, coach Carlos Eduardo Patetuci discussed the challenges posed by the Europeans' defensive organization, his team's improvement in the second half and the importance of the result for the rest of the tournament. “It's an opening match against a European team that plays a very organized game. They set up with a back five at times, switching to a 4-4-2. The emotional factor also made it a very back-and-forth game. With those nerves, we lost the second balls and couldn't sustain control of the game. We would take control and then lose it,” he explained. Patetuci did, however, see a significant improvement in his team during the second half. According to him, Brazil were able to execute the movements laid out in their game plan more consistently and find greater stability in the match. “For an opening match, the most important thing was that in the second half, especially after the substitutions, we improved a lot and were more consistent in our movements and in implementing our style of play. We got the opening win, which was our main objective, to give us peace of mind and confidence for the rest of the competition,” he said. Their next match is against Tanzania on Monday (23). Patetuci is treating the encounter as another final and highlighted the attacking qualities of their opponents, who have skillful players capable of dribbling and improvisation. The coach also pointed to spells of disorganization in the African side as something Brazil intend to exploit. “They're a very strong attacking team, with plenty of dribbling and improvisation too. But at the same time, they struggle to stay organized for long stretches; they lose their shape and become disorganized frequently. We'll take advantage of that with our style of play, looking to be more emotionally composed from the start, implement our game plan, control the game and beat Tanzania too,” he said. Beyond the result, the coach praised the team's competitive spirit and the contribution of the players who came on during the match. For Patetuci, the substitutes' performances underline the importance of being able to count on the entire squad throughout a short, demanding competition. “I was very pleased. Brazil competed hard and fought for every ball. It showed the importance of the collective effort: the players who came on did extremely well, performing at an excellent level. We competed and found our balance in the second half, and that makes us happy because we can count on everyone. Our squad is strong, and we keep moving forward,” he concluded. With three points secured in their opener, Brazil return to action on Monday (23) against Tanzania in the second round of Group I at the U-17 World Cup. The match kicks off at 6 p.m.

top.title: Patience isn't just a virtue for Spurs' Tarris Reed Jr. It's a necessity
top.description: San Antonio Spurs center Tarris Reed Jr. (10) plays in the second half of a preseason NBA game against the Phoenix Suns at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. The Spurs defeated the Suns 123-103. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Spurs rookie Tarris Reed Jr. has learned the hard way the value of patience. As a freshman at Michigan in 2022-23, Reed spent most of every game glued to the end of the bench, only getting his chance to play once the score was out of hand and the outcome decided. "I freaking hated it," Reed said. Three years later, Reed finds himself in a familiar spot with the Spurs. The difference is that the 23-year-old sitting at the end of Mitch Johnson's bench has a much different perspective on what it means to be there. "My mindset has changed," Reed said. "I'm in the NBA now. I get to play these games. I get to be on the best team in the NBA and having fun doing it." Don't get it twisted. Reed still wants to play. It's just now he understands the reward that comes with waiting his turn. In June, the Spurs traded into the bottom of the first round of the draft to select Reed with the No. 26 overall pick. A 6-foot-10, 270-pound mountain of a center, Reed has displayed a nose for rebounding and a knack for wringing every ounce of sweat out of every second of court time he receives. So far, those seconds have been few and far between. Heading into Saturday's game against New Orleans at the Frost Bank Center, Reed had totaled 54 minutes over nine appearances, most of it in mop-up duty. Given the limited playing time, Reed's raw numbers have not jumped off the page. He is averaging 2.0 points and 2.9 rebounds. Look a little closer, however, and it is hard to miss the hint of what he might do with a bigger opportunity. Reed is averaging an astronomical 17.3 rebounds per 36 minutes. "I call him a walking 10 boards," forward Devin Vassell said. "As soon as he gets in the game, I feel like he's getting 10 boards." Reed's patience is being tested at a time when the Spurs are still searching for answers with their second unit. Entering Saturday, San Antonio was 39 points per 100 possessions worse when All-Star Victor Wembanyama went to the bench. Luke Kornet, the 31-year-old veteran charged with filling in for Wembanyama, has had his share of struggles. That leaves an obvious question: What does Reed have to do to earn a more prolonged look at the backup center role? Johnson's answer, perhaps fittingly, is more patience. "I just need him to stay with the process and continue to keep doing what he's doing," Johnson said. "There are times unfortunately when you're on a really good team and you're a younger player fighting to get into the rotation, you can do everything right. It doesn't mean you're going to get what you want." Patience wasn't always Reed's strong suit. But as the 2027 season approaches, one important piece of his future remains unresolved. The 2020 Cup Series champion is entering the final year of his current contract with Hendrick, and no extension beyond 2027 has been announced. top.title: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Called Out for ‘Humiliating’ Decision
top.description: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones Getty There’s no question that the press conference held by Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Thursday of this week was decidedly uncomfortable. He conceded he was disappointed in the fact that his play-calling duties had been stripped, and that he was still the coordinator but in name only. The team moved all of the play-calling to veteran coach Mike Pettine, which makes Parker the coordinator with little to coordinate. It’s a situation in which it is easy to be sympathetic to Parker. At the same time, Parker was a disaster running the defense which, to be fair, has been battered by injury and did not get enough real investment from the team throughout the offseason. Still, Parker is the coordinator and the fact that this group can’t seem to cover receivers or tackle or defend the run ultimately falls on him. Cowboys Don’t Want to Pay Christian Parker After Firing Him? So you can’t hold it against the Cowboys for making a change but you can hold it against them for taking half measures. Keeping Parker on staff while leaving him enfeebled is awkward at best or, as veteran NFL insider Mike Florio said, “humiliating” at worst. And in the end, what it probably comes down to team owner Jerry Jones being penurious with his staff. The Cowboys took away defensive coordinator Christian Parker's play-calling duties but didn't fire him. Probably because Jerry Jones doesn't want to pay the buyout. pic.twitter.com/pI4BO38gTD — PFT Live (@PFT_Live) November 20, 2026 Said Florio during his “PFT” podcast : “ It is impossible not to look at this and suspect that Jerry Jones is hoping he will quit so he doesn’t have to buy him out. I think the best interests of the football team are served by firing Christian Parker and avoiding any confusion in the locker room, who’s really in charge, I am loyal to Christian Parker, well I’m loyal to Mike Pettine—you don’t need that. You just move on, like you would for a coach. “ This fits with the reputation that he does not like to pay coaches to not work. Go ahead and fire him, it is better for your team. He doesn’t want to be there at this point, it is humiliating. “ Parker will be on the sideline, with Pettine, as the Cowboys face the Titans on Sunday in Arlington at 1 p.m. ET. nigeria.description: Carlos Alcaraz rallied past Ben Shelton on Saturday to book his spot in the ATP Finals title match, where he will meet world number one Alexander Zverev as he bids to lift the trophy for the first time. The world number three showed signs of vulnerability but fought through to beat the American 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (7/1). He will play Zverev in Sunday’s decider, after the two-time Finals champion beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (7/0), 6-4 in the other last-four match-up. Alcaraz lost to Italian Jannik Sinner in the season-ender’s showpiece match last year and will aim to go one better this time around in Turin. He has been dealing with a left-thigh injury since Wednesday but, playing with his leg heavily strapped, he extended his winning streak to 13 matches, a run that includes title-winning campaigns in Vienna and Paris. However, it was a hard-fought victory as the Spaniard struggled to play with his usual freedom before pulling through in just over two hours. “I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning because I didn’t start the match the way that I wanted to, to be honest,” said the seven-time Grand Slam winner. “But I’m just happy that I came back in the second set… and ended up playing good tennis.” Having dropped only 15 games across his three round-robin matches without once losing his own serve, Alcaraz was broken in his very first service game against Shelton. The 23-year-old quickly fell behind 3-0 and was unable to claw his way back into the set. In the second frame, Alcaraz upped his level, gaining the upper hand by breaking to lead 5-3 before levelling at one set all. The deciding set remained tight, with neither player facing a break point, forcing the match into a tie-break. Shelton faltered with two unforced errors allowing the Spaniard to pull ahead 5-1, a deficit from which the American could not recover. “I think the third set was even closer. I think he raised the level a little bit from the second set, myself as well,” said Alcaraz. “Great points, great games, and just happy to play great tennis in the tie-breaker… I’m excited for tomorrow.” Earlier in the month, Alcaraz beat Shelton in the Paris Masters final to win the title for the first time — a measure of revenge on the American who had ended his US Open title defence in September. Alcaraz, who missed a chunk of the season with a wrist issue, will nonetheless be able to end his year on a high if he can next beat the man who took his French Open title during his injury-enforced absence. nigeria.title: Tinubu doing fantastic job on sports infrastructure, says Infantino
nigeria.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for its investment in sports infrastructure, describing its efforts as a “fantastic job” and an indication of Nigeria’s commitment to the future of its young population. Infantino gave the commendation on Saturday while addressing the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in Abuja. The FIFA president urged members of the Nigerian delegation to convey his regards to Tinubu, while acknowledging the contributions of the President and other Nigerian leaders to sports development. “On behalf of President Tinubu, please send him our warmest regards. He is doing together with all of you. Fantastic job here in Nigeria, showing that you are a country projected into the future,” Infantino said. He particularly praised investments in sports facilities, noting that they reflected confidence in the potential of young Nigerians. “We were discussing this yesterday as well, also with the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, my brother Shehu. The investments done in sports facilities infrastructure show that you believe in your youth, in the young girls and the young boys of Nigeria,” he said. “Thank you for that. Congratulations for that,” he added. Infantino also thanked Nigeria for hosting him and his delegation, which included FIFA Secretary-General Mattias Grafström, describing the visit as an opportunity to reconnect with the continent. “Thanks for welcoming me and our delegation with the Secretary-General and the others here at home in Africa, in Abuja. Thank you for your support. It means the world to me,” he said. His remarks followed an inspection of sports infrastructure projects in Nigeria on Friday, including the remodelled Warri City Stadium and the Hussey College mini-stadium and sports complex in Delta State. He also visited the ongoing FIFA Forward Technical Centre project at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja, describing the facility as an investment in the future of Nigerian football. “This is a collaboration between Nigerian football and FIFA for the future of the girls and the boys of Nigeria,” he said. During his visit to the Warri City Stadium, Infantino stressed the importance of developing grassroots sports facilities to ensure that football remained accessible to people across communities. “That’s what football is about. It’s for everyone, everywhere. It’s the big stadiums, it’s the World Cup, but it’s also the smaller stadiums, it’s the proximity,” he said. The FIFA president also expressed appreciation for the reception he received in Nigeria, assuring the country of the world football governing body’s continued support. “I feel so much the love of Africa, the love of Nigeria. I am very happy to be here. You can always count on FIFA. We are not just your partners; we are your family members,” he added. Infantino’s visit also coincided with Nigeria’s endorsement of his bid for another term as FIFA

nigeria.title: Arsenal held by Newcastle rally and lose Raya to injury
nigeria.description: Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw on Saturday. The Gunners led through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes. But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle. Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points. However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise. Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions. Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St. James’ Park. Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title. Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on. Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a £75 million ($98 million) move to the Emirates Stadium In August. The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener. It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek. Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break. Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so. Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level. Suddenly an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks. Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya. That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga. Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell. But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title. Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the right and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek. nigeria.title: 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has described the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC’s decision to postpone the clean-up of the national voters’ register until after the 2027 general elections as a major failure. The party said INEC had four years to prepare for the exercise. However, ADC said the voters’ register is only one of several issues that will determine the credibility of the 2027 elections. They pointed to electronic transmission of results, result collation and compliance with the Electoral Act as other major areas of concern. Speaking to Vanguard, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, said INEC’s failure to clean up the register raised questions about its commitment to conducting credible elections. “This shouldn’t have happened. INEC had four years to prepare and plan for this, and its failure to do so does not suggest that it is taking its responsibilities seriously, particularly the issue of maintaining a credible voters’ register,” he said. Abdullahi, however, said the party would not make the outcome of the 2027 elections depend solely on whether INEC produced a credible voters’ register, noting that previous elections had been conducted despite imperfections in the register. “We do not believe that the credibility of the 2027 general election rests solely on INEC’s ability to produce a credible voters’ register. It would have given everyone greater confidence if the commission had been able to do so, but we are not going to hinge the fate of the 2027 election on that single issue.” He said the ADC was also concerned about how INEC would implement the Electoral Act, particularly the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation process and the duties of electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E. “There are other, more pertinent issues of concern to our party. These include compliance with the Electoral Act, the electronic transmission of results from polling units, the collation of results and the additional responsibilities assigned to electoral officers regarding Forms EC8A and EC8E.” On the possible effect of the voters’ register on the elections, Abdullahi argued that strict compliance with the law, particularly provisions on voter accreditation, could reduce the impact of its shortcomings. “If INEC complies with the Electoral Act, particularly regarding voter accreditation, the shortcomings in the voters’ register may not have as much impact. Problems arise when the commission fails to abide by its own rules and the provisions of the Electoral Act,” he said. He said the ADC was studying possible weaknesses in the electoral process and making arrangements to ensure that its votes were protected. “We know where the loopholes are, and that is why we continue to focus on them and ensure that we make adequate arrangements to protect our votes.” Vanguard News The post 2027 Election: INEC failed on voters’ register – ADC appeared first

nigeria.title: ‘Duty of care’: Players’ union slams Bayern for Musiala comments
nigeria.description: Global players’ union FIFPRO has slammed Bayern Munich for putting pressure on midfielder Jamal Musiala to renegotiate his contract with the Bundesliga club as he recovers from injury. In a statement issued Saturday, the footballers’ union said recent public comments made by Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness, current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge were part of a “coordinated campaign” to put pressure on Musiala. The Bayern bosses had questioned whether Musiala, who missed several matches with a neurological condition earlier in the season and has recently returned from a hamstring injury, should continue to receive his contracted salary. FIFPRO hit out at “a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations”. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” the international union for professional football players said. “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala… Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. “Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.” The 23-year-old Germany international signed a contract extension in February 2025 until 2030 and is among Bayern’s top earners. Musiala missed six months after breaking his ankle at the Club World Cup in the summer of 2025. At the start of the 2026-27 season, Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season. He later revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Speaking Friday after Musiala came off the bench for his first Bayern appearance in two months, Rummenigge suggested the player would not be able to recapture his previous form. “Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” Rummenigge said on Sky Germany. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.” Bayern on Saturday announced record revenues of 988.2 million euros ($1.083 billion) for the 2025-26 season. nigeria.title: China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents
nigeria.description: Standing at the Xi’an International Port Station in northwest China, watching the movement of freight trains preparing to transport goods across borders and continents, I was reminded that economic development is not only about what a country produces. It is also about how efficiently it can move what it produces to the rest of the world. Xi’an occupies an interesting place in China’s history. It was once the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, which connected China to Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe through centuries of trade and cultural exchange. Today, the city is reclaiming that historic role through a modern railway network that connects Chinese manufacturing centres to markets across Europe and Asia. The China-Europe Railway Express is one of the most visible outcomes of China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). Through this network, freight trains transport automobiles, electronics, machinery, textiles, agricultural products and other goods across the Eurasian continent. What makes the initiative particularly interesting is how it has transformed the economic possibilities of a city located thousands of kilometres from the sea. Xi’an has become an important international logistics hub, demonstrating that geographical distance from a coastline does not have to limit a city’s participation in global trade. The railway network has continued to expand. By November 2025, China-Europe freight trains had completed nearly 120,000 journeys, connecting 232 cities in 26 European countries and more than 100 cities in 11 Asian countries. The value of goods transported through the network had reached $426.4 billion by the end of 2024. These are not merely impressive transportation figures. They represent an evolving system of economic connectivity, linking manufacturers, suppliers, distributors and consumers across national borders. Beyond transportation: The economics of connectivity The significance of the railway goes beyond moving containers from one destination to another. It creates opportunities for businesses to reach markets faster, diversify their supply chains and reduce their dependence on a single transportation route. Rail freight offers an important middle ground between air and sea transportation. While it is generally more expensive than shipping by sea, it can be considerably faster. For certain categories of goods, particularly machinery, automobile components, electronics and other time-sensitive products, that difference can be commercially significant. nigeria.title: REC confirms 2.8m registered voters in Edo
nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Obo Effanga yest said that the state currently has 2.8 million registered voters. According to him, the last registration exercise raised the figure adding that the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Giving an update on the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) collection in Benin City, Effanga said a total of 23,401 cards had been collected across the state since distribution commenced on October 9. He explained that the figure comprised 6,319 old PVCs, 5,128 newly produced cards and 11,954 PVCs relating to transfers. Effanga noted, “The state currently has 2.8 million registered voters after the last registration exercise. However, the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the national body.” The REC disclosed that PVCs for voters who registered during the first and second phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise were currently available for collection at INEC offices across the 18 local government areas of the state. The Resident Commissioner said the commission was currently working towards ensuring a smooth electoral process. Speaking on the mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, the REC said the exercise would be conducted in 384 polling units across the state. He said two polling units were selected from each of the 192 wards also known as registration areas for the mock exercise. “The exercise would provide an opportunity to test the commission’s electoral technology and assess the readiness of its personnel ahead of the elections. “The state office had submitted the list of proposed polling units to the commission’s headquarters for approval,” he added. He said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System would be deployed during the exercise to demonstrate how voters are accredited, how results are captured and how they are transmitted to the INEC Result Viewing Portal. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. entertainment.title: Tochukwu Ekoh: What My Friend’s Passing Taught Me About Kindness
entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. (Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) NORMAN, Okla. - Mike Elko has opted for a change in quarterback for Texas A& M 's final road game of a disappointing 2026 season. Brady Hart's first career start Saturday against Oklahoma comes one week after he received his most meaningful playing time of the season. The sophomore quarterback entered the Aggies' 22-7 loss to Tennessee last week with under 3 minutes remaining and completed two of his three pass attempts for 22 yards before throwing an interception. Elko took responsibility for the offense after the loss, calling it "inept" and "completely non-functional" while pushing back against the idea that the problems could be attributed solely to Reed. The San Francisco 49ers have needed wide receiver help this season, as they've dealt with a ridiculous string of injuries. But heading into Week 11, it appears they're getting healthy. Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel have been back, and now Mike Evans appears set to play in Sunday Night Football against the Minnesota Vikings . The return of these WRs, along with the trade for Keenan Allen, has really shaken up this WR room. One fallout of this WR room improving and getting healthier is a veteran wide receiver who's spent time with the Buffalo Bills and New Orleans Saints , Brandin Cooks, who the 49ers announced on Saturday was being waived prior to Week 11. 49ers waive WR Brandin Cooks prior to Week 11 "The following player has been waived: WR Brandin Cooks," the 49ers announced. "In addition, CB Nate Hobbs game status has been downgraded from questionable to out." San Francisco's WR room is getting healthier, and that's led the team to move on from Cooks this season. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Demarcus Robinson, Keenan Allen, Jordan Watkins, and Jacob Cowing are all healthy for the 49ers right now. While this is an older WR room that does need depth, the 49ers do not need a seventh WR in Cooks, especially with De'Zhuan Stribling potentially coming back later this season as well. Cooks played in five games for the 49ers this season, catching five of his 10 targets for 58 yards and a touchdown. The 49ers are Cooks' seventh NFL franchise, and the most recent one after spending 2025 with the Saints and Bills. If this is it for Cooks, he's had an incredible career. But with plenty of WR-needy teams around the NFL, Cooks, at 33 years old, could realistically sign somewhere this season and chase 10,000 receiving yards. A return to the Los Angeles Rams would make sense. But with the 49ers getting healthier in the wide receiver room, they've decided to move on from Cooks. He'll hit waivers, where he could be claimed by a team. If he clears, he'll be a free agent and could choose any team, including the 49ers, to sign with. sports.title: U17 World Cup: Patetuci hails opening win and squad strength
sports.description: U17 World Cup: Patetuci hails opening win and squad strength Coach pleased with the team's approach Credits: Nelson Terme /CBF Brazil's men's U-17 national team opened their World Cup campaign with a 2-1 win over Ireland on Saturday (21) in Doha, Qatar. After the match, coach Carlos Eduardo Patetuci discussed the challenges posed by the Europeans' defensive organization, his team's improvement in the second half and the importance of the result for the rest of the tournament. “It's an opening match against a European team that plays a very organized game. They set up with a back five at times, switching to a 4-4-2. The emotional factor also made it a very back-and-forth game. With those nerves, we lost the second balls and couldn't sustain control of the game. We would take control and then lose it,” he explained. Patetuci did, however, see a significant improvement in his team during the second half. According to him, Brazil were able to execute the movements laid out in their game plan more consistently and find greater stability in the match. “For an opening match, the most important thing was that in the second half, especially after the substitutions, we improved a lot and were more consistent in our movements and in implementing our style of play. We got the opening win, which was our main objective, to give us peace of mind and confidence for the rest of the competition,” he said. Their next match is against Tanzania on Monday (23). Patetuci is treating the encounter as another final and highlighted the attacking qualities of their opponents, who have skillful players capable of dribbling and improvisation. The coach also pointed to spells of disorganization in the African side as something Brazil intend to exploit. “They're a very strong attacking team, with plenty of dribbling and improvisation too. But at the same time, they struggle to stay organized for long stretches; they lose their shape and become disorganized frequently. We'll take advantage of that with our style of play, looking to be more emotionally composed from the start, implement our game plan, control the game and beat Tanzania too,” he said. Beyond the result, the coach praised the team's competitive spirit and the contribution of the players who came on during the match. For Patetuci, the substitutes' performances underline the importance of being able to count on the entire squad throughout a short, demanding competition. “I was very pleased. Brazil competed hard and fought for every ball. It showed the importance of the collective effort: the players who came on did extremely well, performing at an excellent level. We competed and found our balance in the second half, and that makes us happy because we can count on everyone. Our squad is strong, and we keep moving forward,” he concluded. With three points secured in their opener, Brazil return to action on Monday (23) against Tanzania in the second round of Group I at the U-17 World Cup. The match kicks off at 6 p.m.

sports.title: Patience isn't just a virtue for Spurs' Tarris Reed Jr. It's a necessity
sports.description: San Antonio Spurs center Tarris Reed Jr. (10) plays in the second half of a preseason NBA game against the Phoenix Suns at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Wednesday, Oct. 14, 2026. The Spurs defeated the Suns 123-103. (Sam Owens/San Antonio Express-News) Spurs rookie Tarris Reed Jr. has learned the hard way the value of patience. As a freshman at Michigan in 2022-23, Reed spent most of every game glued to the end of the bench, only getting his chance to play once the score was out of hand and the outcome decided. "I freaking hated it," Reed said. Three years later, Reed finds himself in a familiar spot with the Spurs. The difference is that the 23-year-old sitting at the end of Mitch Johnson's bench has a much different perspective on what it means to be there. "My mindset has changed," Reed said. "I'm in the NBA now. I get to play these games. I get to be on the best team in the NBA and having fun doing it." Don't get it twisted. Reed still wants to play. It's just now he understands the reward that comes with waiting his turn. In June, the Spurs traded into the bottom of the first round of the draft to select Reed with the No. 26 overall pick. A 6-foot-10, 270-pound mountain of a center, Reed has displayed a nose for rebounding and a knack for wringing every ounce of sweat out of every second of court time he receives. So far, those seconds have been few and far between. Heading into Saturday's game against New Orleans at the Frost Bank Center, Reed had totaled 54 minutes over nine appearances, most of it in mop-up duty. Given the limited playing time, Reed's raw numbers have not jumped off the page. He is averaging 2.0 points and 2.9 rebounds. Look a little closer, however, and it is hard to miss the hint of what he might do with a bigger opportunity. Reed is averaging an astronomical 17.3 rebounds per 36 minutes. "I call him a walking 10 boards," forward Devin Vassell said. "As soon as he gets in the game, I feel like he's getting 10 boards." Reed's patience is being tested at a time when the Spurs are still searching for answers with their second unit. Entering Saturday, San Antonio was 39 points per 100 possessions worse when All-Star Victor Wembanyama went to the bench. Luke Kornet, the 31-year-old veteran charged with filling in for Wembanyama, has had his share of struggles. That leaves an obvious question: What does Reed have to do to earn a more prolonged look at the backup center role? Johnson's answer, perhaps fittingly, is more patience. "I just need him to stay with the process and continue to keep doing what he's doing," Johnson said. "There are times unfortunately when you're on a really good team and you're a younger player fighting to get into the rotation, you can do everything right. It doesn't mean you're going to get what you want." Patience wasn't always Reed's strong suit. sports.title: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Called Out for ‘Humiliating’ Decision
sports.description: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones Getty There’s no question that the press conference held by Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Thursday of this week was decidedly uncomfortable. He conceded he was disappointed in the fact that his play-calling duties had been stripped, and that he was still the coordinator but in name only. The team moved all of the play-calling to veteran coach Mike Pettine, which makes Parker the coordinator with little to coordinate. It’s a situation in which it is easy to be sympathetic to Parker. At the same time, Parker was a disaster running the defense which, to be fair, has been battered by injury and did not get enough real investment from the team throughout the offseason. Still, Parker is the coordinator and the fact that this group can’t seem to cover receivers or tackle or defend the run ultimately falls on him. Cowboys Don’t Want to Pay Christian Parker After Firing Him? So you can’t hold it against the Cowboys for making a change but you can hold it against them for taking half measures. Keeping Parker on staff while leaving him enfeebled is awkward at best or, as veteran NFL insider Mike Florio said, “humiliating” at worst. And in the end, what it probably comes down to team owner Jerry Jones being penurious with his staff. The Cowboys took away defensive coordinator Christian Parker's play-calling duties but didn't fire him. Probably because Jerry Jones doesn't want to pay the buyout. pic.twitter.com/pI4BO38gTD — PFT Live (@PFT_Live) November 20, 2026 Said Florio during his “PFT” podcast : “ It is impossible not to look at this and suspect that Jerry Jones is hoping he will quit so he doesn’t have to buy him out. I think the best interests of the football team are served by firing Christian Parker and avoiding any confusion in the locker room, who’s really in charge, I am loyal to Christian Parker, well I’m loyal to Mike Pettine—you don’t need that. You just move on, like you would for a coach. “ This fits with the reputation that he does not like to pay coaches to not work. Go ahead and fire him, it is better for your team. He doesn’t want to be there at this point, it is humiliating. “ Parker will be on the sideline, with Pettine, as the Cowboys face the Titans on Sunday in Arlington at 1 p.m. ET. sports.title: Steelers Get Much-Needed Reinforcement Ahead of Eagles Game
sports.description: Max Hurleman at Steelers OTA's on June 9th 2026 - Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers just received some positive news from their wide receiver corps ahead of their Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Pittsburgh Steelers have elevated wide receiver Max Hurleman from the practice squad to the active roster. Hurleman was removed from the practice squad injured list on Wednesday. He’s been receiving high praise lately. He even got a shoutout from quarterback Aaron Rodgers . For Hurleman, hearing his name mentioned by Rodgers was indicative that all of his hard work is paying off. “It’s pretty cool, honestly,” Hurleman said. “I’m super thankful to be in his good graces, and have him think of me that way, and to potentially be lobbying on my behalf, that’s super cool and we’ll see what happens obviously. But it’s a good feeling to know that he trusts me and thinks I deserve a shot.” After spending the past two seasons on the practice squad, Hurleman, 25, could potentially play in his first regular-season game since joining the Steelers in 2025 after going undrafted. In the 2025 preseason, Hurleman played in three games in which he recorded three receptions for 33 yards and one touchdown, including a two-catch, 29-yard, one-touchdown debut against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The former Notre Dame product made headlines when coach Mike McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers mentioned Hurleman in a recent press conference, indicating their confidence in him. After participating in the Steelers’ OTAs and in training camp, Hurleman was waived as part of final roster cuts on Aug. 30; however, he was re-signed to the practice squad the following day. The Steelers have been dealing with injuries to their receivers room for much of the season. Veteran receiver and new addition to the team, Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on injured reserve on Oct.10 after aggravating a left foot injury/plantar fasciitis. He had his 21-day practice window opened in mid-November, and he was a full participant by Thursday/Friday of Week 11 and is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game at Philadelphia, and third-year receiver Roman Wilson suffered a broken middle finger and dislocated ring finger on his left hand during the second quarter of the Week 5 game against the Indianapolis Colts, landing on injured reserve on Oct.17. sports.title: Bills Could Pick Rookie CB Over Tre’Davious White Amid Secondary Injuries
sports.description: Joe Brady praises DJ Moore after his return from injury. Getty The Buffalo Bills are headed to their divisional showdown against the Miami Dolphins with an ailing secondary, and could tape a standout rookie for help. The Bills ruled out starting cornerback Christian Benford for the game and listed cornerback Dee Alford and safety Damar Hamlin as questionable. The Bills are expected to tap the practice squad for some help, and could pass over the recently added Tre’Davious White. Bills Could Turn to Kani Walker SI.com writer Ralph Ventre noted that the Bills are thin at cornerback heading into Sunday’s game, likely forcing them to make some changes and bring up some help. While Ventre noted that the Bills could call on White, the veteran and team’s former first-round pick in 2017, they have also shown faith in rookie Kani Walker. “While cornerback Maxwell Hairston will presumably start opposite second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun, the Bills have no other true outside cornerbacks on the 53-man roster,” Ventre wrote. “Although Alford can flip outside if need be, Buffalo seems best served by making a practice squad elevation with veteran Tre’Davious White and undrafted rookie Kani Walker both viable options.” The Bills elevated Walker for their Oct. 3 game against the New England Patriots, where he made one assisted tackle. Tre’Davious White Could Appear in First Game This Season Other Bills insiders believe White will get the call-up from the practice squad. The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia noted that the Bills signed him to the practice squad because of his steady presence in the secondary, starting 16 games last season and helping rookie Maxwell Hairston in his development. “Tre’Davious White is on the practice squad, and this is why the Bills brought him back in the first place,” Buscagalia wrote . “That’s also why they decided against going after another veteran cornerback in the trade market. … “If Benford has to miss any time, the Bills might need White to play as early as next week. And if it goes well enough, maybe even earn a bigger role as the year goes on.” The Bills initially cut ties with White in March 2024, but signed him again the next offseason. At the time, White said he told his agent that he would only return to play in Buffalo. The team could also choose to elevate both Walker and White for the game, giving more depth to a secondary that will be missing some key players. technology.title: AWS got hit by an outage too. Here's why you didn't hear about it
technology.description: My editor asked me this week "why is everything except AWS breaking?" It's a great question! They haven't been in the headlines! In fact, as they are wont to do, AWS spokesperson Patrick Neighorn g ot salty to a reporter about how unreliable Downdetector is when it started showing them as impacted. If you'll permit me a small digression, this stems from a misunderstanding of what Downdetector is for. Historically the AWS status site was so hilariously slow to reflect the lived customer experience that some jackass (me) built a rewriter that sits at stop.lying.cloud to make it a smidgen more realistic. As a result, the question people are really trying to answer when they visit Downdetector is "my app just broke; is it my crappy code or is there a global event going on?" There are mitigations for both, but they look nothing alike. AWS view crowdsourced reports of the form "the internet is broken, must be AWS" as a stain upon their honor. In fact, it's a badge of their own success, as "the internet" and "AWS" have become inextricably linked in people's minds. But back to my editor's question, "why didn't AWS go down?" Easy: it did. Everything breaks, all the time, including the narrative AWS now has 34 generally available commercial regions, of which two are currently smoking craters due to the Iran conflict. Each of these has hundreds of services that AWS offers to customers, of which a dozen or so are high quality, if I'm being characteristically uncharitable. They experience degradation in various ways, and they go largely unnoticed. But on November 15, AWS confirmed an incident that disrupted 11 of those ~12 good services in their oldest and most important region, us-east-1. At 3:05 AM PST, they stated that they started seeing sign-up errors, authentication issues, and connectivity issues. Five minutes later engineers were engaged. Not to be outdone, their status page swung into action after a leisurely coffee, and posted its first indication of an incident 93 minutes later. (See previous comments on stop.lying.cloud ). The all-clear showed up at 6:53 AM. Every site has downtime. Sometimes it blows up publicly, other times nobody seems to notice. Heck, AWS said in September that it had experienced permanent data loss in its two smoking craters, but after that news cycle passed I haven't heard a thing about it. I do think it's patently unreasonable to blame them for this specific problem; "acts of war" are kinda hard to predict from the corporate planning meeting. A few things combined to help AWS out on November 15. First, it was pre-dawn Pacific time on Sunday. Most of us slept through it; my kids aren't even up that early. Further, the services that were most impacted (IAM Identity Center) were for engineers signing in to AWS accounts, not consumers staring at an app that stopped working. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

science.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest big-screen adventure
science.description:
Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. After studying physics at university, he became a journalist, swapped science fact for science fiction, and hit the jackpot when he joined the team at SFX, the UK's biggest sci-fi and fantasy magazine. He liked it so much he stayed there for 12 years, four of them as editor. 

He's since gone freelance and passes his time writing about "Star Wars", "Star Trek" and superheroes for the likes of SFX, Total Film, TechRadar and GamesRadar+. He has met five Doctors, two Starfleet captains and one Luke Skywalker, and once sat in the cockpit of "Red Dwarf"'s Starbug.  

Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. He even calls Worf — not a man renowned for dodging a fight — a coward, prompting the Klingon to respond that, "If you were any other man, I would kill you where you stand." Ouch. But following some impassioned talk about making the Borg "pay for what they've done", he's finally talked down from his rage by 21st-century stowaway Lily Sloane (Alfre Woodard). She points out that his Moby-Dick-esque obsession is on the verge of going full Ahab, and he eventually sees sense, issuing the order to abandon the Enterprise and destroy the hive. It's a masterclass showcasing the ever-brilliant Stewart's impressive range, as the out-of-control captain's rarely seen temper reaches fever pitch, before normal service is resumed. His subsequent apology to Worf — "As a matter of fact, I think you're the bravest man I've ever known" — is simply perfect. And just as the franchise's zenith, "The Wrath of Khan", is built around Kirk and Khan's decades-old feud, "First Contact" is precision engineered to get the most out of Jean-Luc. This was the right "Star Trek" at the right time, a film that put "TNG"'s greatest villains on a collision course with the origins of Starfleet.
